title: Why Matassa dislikes Jerry Wexler: the Professor Longhair eulogy
summary: He calls Wexler a terrible person, citing his eulogy at Professor Longhair's funeral when he never did anything for Longhair.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: And you said, you said you're not a Jerry Wexler fan, is there? No. And he.
Well, I think, I think he's a terrible human being.
But, you know, and I don't mind being on tape about it. Please. This is the forum.
Go ahead. But that's another story. And I don't want to rehash that.
There's another, something he said, something he did.

It's things he said and things he did. For instance. I'll give you a for instance. Please. He showed up at Professor Longhair's funeral and did a eulogy. Right. Yeah. I could have thrown up. Okay. He was a guy who never, ever did anything for Longhair. And stood up there like he had been his bosom buddy. Standing by him with his hand on his shoulder and his, you know, the wind beneath his wings kind of thing. And he never was any of those things.
I mean. Nothing. If there was anything he might have done, he didn't. It didn't happen. Whether he was aware and could have and didn't, I don't know.
Well, he keeps saying, oh, he did the Tipitina session.
But he didn't do anything for Longhair. You know what I'm saying?
